title: Dyslipidaemia: risk categories, LDL-C goals and lipid-lowering therapy (India, CSI)
subject: cardiology
setting: Outpatient clinic, cardiology, diabetes clinic, post-ACS discharge
summary: Use non-fasting lipids, place the patient in one of five CSI risk categories and treat to LDL-C and non-HDL-C goals (below 55 and 85 mg/dL in very high risk). Start with a statin, add ezetimibe early (at initiation after ACS), then bempedoic acid, a PCSK9 inhibitor or inclisiran if the goal is not met by 4 weeks.

sections.title: Assess risk (CSI five categories)
items: Measure a non-fasting lipid profile (total, LDL, HDL and non-HDL cholesterol, triglycerides) for risk estimation and treatment; a fasting sample is not required. Check every adult by age 18. Measure Lp(a) at least once in a lifetime.
Low risk: no risk factors. Moderate risk: one of smoking or tobacco use, hypertension, diabetes, or family history of premature CAD (men under 55, women under 60).
High risk: 2 or more risk factors without ASCVD, chronic kidney disease, diabetes for more than 10 years, or heterozygous FH.
Very high risk: clinical ASCVD (coronary, cerebrovascular or peripheral), diabetes for more than 20 years, HeFH with ASCVD, or coronary imaging showing more than 50% stenosis in 2 vessels.
Extremely high risk: recurrent vascular events, or ASCVD with genetic dyslipidaemia (FH or high Lp(a)).

Look for secondary causes: hypothyroidism, poorly controlled diabetes, Cushing syndrome or long-term glucocorticoids, immunosuppressants, anabolic steroid misuse, obesity and PCOS. Ensure euthyroid state before starting a statin.

sections.title: Goals and statin therapy
items: LDL-C goals: low and moderate risk below 100 mg/dL; high risk below 70 mg/dL; very high risk below 55 mg/dL. Non-HDL-C (co-primary goal): below 130, 130, 100 and 85 mg/dL respectively. Triglycerides below 150 mg/dL and Lp(a) below 50 mg/dL are desirable at all levels.

Statins are first-line in every risk group. High intensity: atorvastatin 40 to 80 mg or rosuvastatin 20 to 40 mg daily. Moderate intensity: atorvastatin 10 to 20 mg, rosuvastatin 5 to 10 mg or pitavastatin 2 to 4 mg. Low intensity: atorvastatin 5 mg or pitavastatin 1 mg.
Indians may respond to lower statin doses and may be more prone to adverse effects: titrate to the goal rather than to a fixed dose.
Atherogenic dyslipidaemia (high triglycerides, low HDL-C, small dense LDL) is common in Indians: start a high-intensity statin; many will also need ezetimibe.

Routine baseline or follow-up CK and liver enzyme monitoring is not recommended. Transaminase rise up to 3 times normal is not a contraindication. For muscle symptoms, reduce the dose, pause and re-challenge, or switch to a lower-potency statin.

sections.title: ACS and established ASCVD
items: ACS: check a non-fasting lipid profile on arrival; aim for LDL-C below 55 mg/dL as early as possible (hit hard and early).
Start high-intensity statin plus ezetimibe 10 mg at initiation after ACS, because high-dose statin alone often fails to reach the goal.
If LDL-C is not below 55 mg/dL at 4 weeks, add bempedoic acid, a PCSK9 inhibitor or inclisiran.

Chronic coronary syndrome, stroke survivors and peripheral arterial disease are very high risk: LDL-C below 55 mg/dL and non-HDL-C below 85 mg/dL. Add ezetimibe and/or bempedoic acid if not at goal or statin-intolerant.
PCSK9 inhibitors are effective but costly: reserve for very high-risk patients not at goal on maximally tolerated statin with or without ezetimibe.

sections.title: Hypertriglyceridaemia
items: Treat the cause (obesity, diabetes, alcohol, hypothyroidism, drugs) and restrict excess calories, sugars, refined carbohydrates, fried food and trans fats; use a statin to reach the non-HDL-C goal.

Triglycerides 150 to 499 mg/dL: no role for fibrates. In diabetes (age 40 or over) or ASCVD with persistent high triglycerides after lifestyle and glucose control, icosapent ethyl 2 g twice daily may be considered.
Fasting triglycerides above 500 mg/dL: fenofibrate 145 mg once daily, mainly to prevent acute pancreatitis.
In type 2 diabetes with mixed dyslipidaemia, fenofibrate added to a statin may be used; do not combine fibrates with statins in CKD or after transplantation.

sections.title: Diabetes, CKD, pregnancy and other groups
items: Diabetes: LDL-C below 55 mg/dL with ASCVD, diabetes for more than 20 years or multiple risk factors; below 70 mg/dL with any risk factor; below 100 mg/dL for new-onset diabetes without risk factors.

CKD: statin with or without ezetimibe if eGFR is below 60 mL/min/1.73 m2, or albumin to creatinine ratio 3 mg/mmol or more for at least 3 months. Do not start statins in most haemodialysis patients without ASCVD, but continue if already taking them. No ezetimibe monotherapy.

Pregnancy and breastfeeding: statins, ezetimibe and bempedoic acid are contraindicated; diet first, and bile acid sequestrants or omega-3 fatty acids if needed. Avoid statins in women planning pregnancy or without reliable contraception.

Elderly (70 and over): individualise primary prevention, start low and titrate; in secondary prevention use the same goals as younger adults. Over 80 years, primary prevention depends on judgement and preference.
Liver: statins are first-line in MASLD, but contraindicated in decompensated cirrhosis and acute liver failure. HIV: pitavastatin preferred; avoid simvastatin with protease inhibitors.
Young adults: start a statin if LDL-C is 190 mg/dL or more on repeat testing; young adults with ASCVD need LDL-C below 55 mg/dL.

sections.title: Familial hypercholesterolaemia and Lp(a)
items: Suspect FH with very high LDL-C or premature CAD. Dutch Lipid Clinic Network score above 8 is definite and 6 to 8 probable FH; genetic testing confirms. Cascade-screen relatives.

Adult HeFH: high-intensity statin plus ezetimibe from the start; LDL-C goal below 70 mg/dL (primary prevention) or below 55 mg/dL (with ASCVD); add bempedoic acid, a PCSK9 inhibitor or inclisiran if needed.

Children with HeFH: statin to an LDL-C target below 130 mg/dL; drug therapy is best avoided below 10 years except in severe primary hyperlipidaemia. Homozygous FH (LDL-C often above 500 mg/dL) needs specialist combination therapy.
Elevated Lp(a) (above 50 mg/dL or 125 nmol/L, about 1 in 4 South Asians) has no approved specific therapy: control all other risk factors aggressively and test first-degree relatives.

sections.title: Lifestyle
items: At least 150 minutes a week of moderate-intensity activity on at least 5 days, plus resistance training 3 times a week; start low and build up every 2 to 4 weeks. Yoga is encouraged.

Keep carbohydrates to about 50% of calories, limit sugars, refined grains, sugar-sweetened drinks and processed foods; avoid trans fats, re-used frying oil and palm oil; prefer a mix of MUFA and PUFA oils.
Daily: 3 to 5 servings of vegetables and legumes, 2 to 3 of fruit, 1 of nuts, 2 to 3 of whole grains; sodium below 2.3 g. Restrict alcohol; it is not advised for heart protection.
Stop smoking and all tobacco; reach and keep a healthy weight.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Waiting for a fasting sample, which delays treatment after ACS.
Stopping at a statin alone after ACS instead of adding ezetimibe from the start.
Using fibrates for moderate hypertriglyceridaemia, or fibrates with statins in CKD.
Stopping statins for mildly raised transaminases (below 3 times normal) or in MASLD.
Ignoring non-HDL-C in patients with high triglycerides, where LDL-C underestimates risk.

drugs.name: Atorvastatin
drugs.dose: High intensity 40 to 80 mg; moderate 10 to 20 mg; low 5 mg; orally once daily
drugs.notes: Contraindicated in pregnancy, breastfeeding, decompensated cirrhosis.

drugs.name: Rosuvastatin
drugs.dose: High intensity 20 to 40 mg; moderate 5 to 10 mg; orally once daily

drugs.name: Pitavastatin
drugs.dose: Moderate 2 to 4 mg; low 1 mg; orally once daily

drugs.name: Ezetimibe
drugs.notes: At initiation after ACS and in HeFH; lowers LDL-C about 15% alone. Not in moderate to severe hepatic insufficiency.

drugs.name: Bempedoic acid
drugs.notes: Add-on or statin intolerance; about 25% LDL-C fall alone. Raises uric acid. Not in pregnancy.

drugs.name: Evolocumab
drugs.dose: 140 mg SC every 2 weeks, or 420 mg SC once a month
drugs.notes: About 50 to 60% LDL-C reduction; very high risk not at goal.

drugs.name: Inclisiran
drugs.dose: 284 mg SC on day 1 and day 90, then every 6 months
drugs.notes: About 50% LDL-C reduction; adjunct to statin in ASCVD and HeFH.

drugs.name: Fenofibrate
drugs.notes: Fasting triglycerides above 500 mg/dL. Contraindicated in acute liver and severe renal disease.

drugs.name: Icosapent ethyl
drugs.notes: Persistent triglycerides on statin in diabetes or ASCVD.

drugs.name: Colesevelam
drugs.notes: Add-on; bile acid sequestrants are the only lipid drugs considered safe in pregnancy and lactation.

sources.title: CSI clinical practice guidelines for dyslipidemia management: executive summary (Indian Heart Journal 76 Suppl 1)
